title: Trump begins a 32-day midterm campaign tour in Texas and Oklahoma
summary: President Donald Trump began a 32-day campaign tour with stops in Texas and Oklahoma as Republicans campaign to retain their congressional majorities.

title: Trump plans campaign stops in competitive Ohio and Nebraska races
summary: Reuters reported that Trump is scheduled to move from Republican-leaning states toward competitive regions including Ohio and Nebraska during his midterm campaign tour.

title: Texas Senate race draws national attention as Trump campaigns with Ken Paxton
summary: Trump appeared with Republican Senate candidate Ken Paxton in Texas, where the race is among the contests receiving national attention.

title: Reuters reports Democrats are expanding the Senate map into traditionally Republican states
summary: Reuters reported that Democratic campaigns are competitive in several states that Donald Trump won by double digits in 2024, including Kentucky, Texas and Kansas.

title: Kentucky Senate race becomes part of Democrats' expanded 2026 target map
summary: Reuters reported that Democrat Charles Booker is challenging Republican Andy Barr in Kentucky as Democrats assess whether to devote resources to the race.

title: Republicans redirect campaign resources toward newly competitive Senate contests
summary: Reuters reported that Republican strategists are redirecting funds from traditional battlegrounds toward seats that have become more competitive.

title: Florida Senate race sees nearly $5 million in Super PAC spending for Ashley Moody
summary: Reuters reported that a Super PAC backed by Ken Griffin has spent nearly $5 million supporting Republican Senate candidate Ashley Moody in Florida.

title: Congress adjourns until after the November midterms
summary: Congress has adjourned for the campaign period, with lawmakers returning to their home states and districts ahead of the November election.

title: Senate data-center bill fails to advance in a 57–43 vote
summary: A Senate bill addressing data-center electricity costs failed to reach the 60-vote threshold. AP reported that the issue has become part of several 2026 campaign debates.

title: House passes data-center measure 417–3 before lawmakers leave Washington
summary: The House had previously passed the data-center measure by 417–3; the Senate later failed to advance it before the midterm campaign period.

title: Georgia election board delays vote on proposed ballot-privacy change
summary: Georgia's State Election Board did not immediately adopt a Republican-backed proposal concerning a software flaw that could allow ballots to be linked to individual voters.

title: Georgia board urges Secretary of State to address voting-system software flaw
summary: AP reported that the Georgia board separately passed a resolution urging the Secretary of State to address the software issue and improve voting software.

title: Early voting begins at two downtown Chicago locations
summary: Chicago opened two downtown early-voting locations on October 1 for the November general election, with additional locations expected to open later in the month.

title: Texas voter-registration deadline approaches before the November election
summary: The Texas Tribune reported that October 5 is the voter-registration deadline for the November 3, 2026 election in Texas.

title: Early voting is available to all voters in 47 states and Washington, D.C.
summary: The Center for Election Innovation & Research reported that 47 states and Washington, D.C. offer early in-person voting to all voters, with dates varying by jurisdiction.

title: Most states begin 2026 early in-person voting in October
summary: The research center reported that most states begin early in-person voting in mid-October, while the earliest statewide starts occur in September.

title: Supreme Court rejects Trump's bid to restrict mail ballots before midterms
summary: AP reported that the Supreme Court rejected the administration's effort to impose new restrictions on mail ballots ahead of the midterm elections.

title: Federal judge blocks withholding of counterterrorism funds over election procedures
summary: A federal judge ruled that the administration could not withhold counterterrorism funding to pressure states into changing election procedures.

title: Supreme Court temporarily allows federal voter-eligibility database use
summary: AP reported that the Supreme Court temporarily allowed the administration to use an expanded federal voter-eligibility database while litigation continues.

title: Federal judge rules 1996 noncitizen-voting law unconstitutional in one Florida case
summary: A Miami federal judge dismissed one case and ruled that the federal law used to prosecute the defendant was unconstitutional; Reuters noted that the ruling applies to that case.

title: AP reports DHS says it does not plan mass ICE deployment at polling places
summary: The Department of Homeland Security said it does not plan to deploy immigration-enforcement officers en masse to polling places during the midterms.

title: 2026 House and Senate campaign spending reaches about $1.9 billion through August
summary: USAFacts, using Federal Election Commission data, reported that House and Senate candidates had spent about $1.9 billion on the 2026 midterm races through August.

title: Midterm advertising spending passes $1.5 billion
summary: The Washington Post reported that advertising spending in 2026 House and Senate races had surpassed $1.5 billion, based on AdImpact data.

title: Ohio Senate race leads national midterm advertising spending
summary: A Washington Post analysis reported that Ohio's Senate race had the highest advertising spending among the 2026 midterm contests, at about $240 million at the time of the report.
